"US President Donald Trump said a new civil nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia depends on the kingdom normalizing ties with Israel, a condition that could derail a landmark deal his administration finalized just a day earlier.

In a social media post Thursday, Trump also said there would be “no enrichment” of nuclear material. The pact would allow American companies to expand nuclear energy development in a long-coveted market, but it also raised concerns about a lack of guardrails that would prevent Riyadh from enriching uranium to weapons-grade."

Please let us not let yet another nation get involved with nuclear! If the public agrees to open this pandoras box there will be issues for any non-compliance/tensions.

Nuclear reactors cost on average near 8 billion dollars and require 5 to 10 years to construct, while facing strict geographic limits, massive water needs, unique public insurance backing, and long-term waste isolation rules.



Siting restrictions prohibit placement within 5 miles of active seismic fault lines and mandate strict buffer zones away from high-intensity hydraulic fracturing fields. Cooling systems demand 50 million gallons of water daily per reactor, requiring proximity to major rivers, lakes, or oceans with uninterrupted intake rights. Even minutes off is fatal.

Severe accident mitigation requires backup power and active cooling for 72 hours post-shutdown, or the core damage can trigger long-term evacuation zones spanning over up to 1,000 square miles.

Financial liability is capped by federal legislation like the Price-Anderson Act, which forces commercial operators to pool risk up to 15 billion dollars rather than relying entirely on private corporate insurers.

Radioactive spent fuel requires dry cask and deep geological repository isolation for over 240,000 years to let plutonium and minor actinides decay to safe baseline background levels to avoid harm to humans and the environment. These are not optional things to take lightly.

This is not to mention if ever there is war tensions and one of these gets caught up in the beef it could cause a multi decade disaster. Look at Chernobyl and Fukusima Japan. We've had close calls here in the US even enough to close them down.

transcript: President Donald Trump announced that the United States has made a deal with Saudi Arabia in regard to their development of a civilian nuclear program. Now, what really stood out about this deal was the fact that it started, or at least the negotiations for it began under the Biden administration, and there was a pretty big caveat that the Biden administration insisted on. We're not going to let you pursue this program unless you normalize relations with Israel. Now, they didn't finish negotiating before Biden's term was up. Trump comes into office, he continues negotiating, and when he announced the deal, there was no mention of normalizing Saudi Arabia's relationship with Israel. So, that caveat seemed to be totally removed. Well, now it looks like Trump got the call from the man who calls the the shots, the actual person who makes the decisions, and that's Benjamin Netanyahu. Uh because today Trump did a complete 180, and it appears he did it unilaterally. So, here's the headline from the Washington Post. Saudi nuclear deal in doubt as Trump adds new condition regarding Israel. A day after the agreement was signed, the president laid out a new requirement that the Saudis normalize relations with Israel. And then in the body of the piece they write that the nuclear deal, which was fiercely opposed by Israel, which you know, you can't have that, is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords, Trump said in a social media post. And then later, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt seemed to confirm that President Donald Trump made this decision unilaterally without even, you know, talking to the Saudis and updating them on what he's demanding. Take a look. >> Just to continue on the Saudi nuclear deal, do the Saudis agree with this interpretation since it wasn't part of the initial agreement, and has the president talked to MBS um since this new condition surfaced? >> As you know, uh the president just put out this statement a few hours ago. I don't believe he's had a call uh with MBS in the hours since. Uh however, this is something that he has raised in previous conversations and has also said many times in the past. >> Now, before the 180 was carried out by President Trump, uh Trita Parsi, the executive vice president of the Quincy Institute, wrote about this civilian and nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia titled uh The US-Saudi nuclear deal makes no sense. How will Washington get Tehran to accept intrusive inspections beyond the JCPOA when Saudi uh is offered enrichment with no IAEA inspections. So, luckily to discuss this story with us today is Trita Parsi, um and we will discuss, you know, what the deal itself actually entails, and I'll get his comments on uh the latest update. Trita, welcome to the show. >> Great to be with you again. >> So, before we even get to the 180 that Trump did this morning, I am very not not curious because I read your piece, but I I would like our audience to be familiar with the arguments that you're making in your piece, especially as it pertains to IAEA inspectors. >> Yes, let me first say something that's very important to understand. This is not a new thing. The Biden administration pushed this very far, and they were really building off of Trump's Abraham Accord. I mean, the only thing they seemed to care about in the Middle East was to get Saudi Arabia to normalize relations with with Israel. And as part of that package, they were entertaining offering um uh security guarantees to Saudi Arabia on the level of NATO, which means that the the United States would be obligated to come and defend Saudi Arabia. And of course, then they the Saudis wanted to have this nuclear uh component to it. And there were moments in which after October 7th when everything on the Abraham Accord kind of went to a standstill, that the Biden administration was contemplating doing just a standalone nuclear deal with the Saudis that would not have required them to normalize relations with Israel because Israelis were paying very little attention to normalization at the time. They [snorts] did recognize, however, that this would be a rather strange deal because the United States would essentially be giving the Saudis nuclear enrichment capability while simultaneously trying to deprive the Iranians from having that same technology and sanctioning them for having that technology. And they also recognized that this deal could give the Saudis a pathway to a nuclear weapon. And as a result, they were looking into, and I write about it on the subsect, they were looking into various ways of dealing with that issue such as actually having American troops guard this nuclear facility and protect it from Saudis so that the Saudis would not be able to take over that facility that was in Saudi Arabia. They were even looking into having self-destruction mechanisms at the site so to make sure that if the Saudis were going in a direction that the US didn't want, it could be destroyed. It's kind of bizarre that if you think that those measures may be necessary, perhaps that would be a hint that this is not a deal you should be doing in the first place. But the Biden administration was so adamant about binding Saudi Arabia to the United States out of a fear that it would be drifting away towards China. And as a result, they were contemplating these things. Now, the Trump administration essentially picked up from where the Biden team left it off. They were offered this and as part of this team, this deal, the inspections would be American inspections. It wouldn't be the international standard of the IAEA going into these nuclear sites. It wouldn't be the same safeguards, etc. Which then creates another complication with um if they simultaneously still desire to make some sort of a nuclear deal with the Iranians because the JCPOA had very intrusive inspections. And if you want to resurrect that or if you even want to go beyond that, which I'm sure the the Trump administration would love to do so they can say they got a better deal than Obama. How can you do then simultaneously give the Saudis something completely different? The whole argument and and you know, [clears throat] Trump administration has tried to deprive the Iranians from enrichment. Now, I don't think that ever would have worked.
